issue.title: Arrow scan of list<dictionary> fails when the first 2048 rows hold no list elements
issue.body:
### What happens?

Scanning an Arrow `list<dictionary<int32, string>>` column fails with an internal error when the first scan chunk (the first 2048 rows) contains zero list elements and later rows contain values:

```
INTERNAL Error: Attempted to dereference unique_ptr that is NULL!
```

In DuckDB-WASM (1.31.0, DuckDB v1.4.0) the same input produces `Failed to cast ArrowTypeInfo, type mismatch (expected: STRING, got: LIST)`, and the database is then invalidated. That is how we hit it in production: `insertArrowFromIPCStream` into a `VARCHAR[]` table.

It passes when the child is plain `utf8`, and when even one of the first 2048 rows holds a value. It also passes when the only all-empty chunk is not the first one.

The cause appears to be the empty-list shortcut in `ArrowToDuckDBList` ([`src/function/table/arrow_conversion.cpp#L228-L233`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/v1.5.6/src/function/table/arrow_conversion.cpp#L228-L233)):

```cpp
if (list_size == 0 && start_offset == 0) {
    D_ASSERT(!child_array.dictionary);
    ArrowToDuckDBConversion::ColumnArrowToDuckDB(child_vector, child_array, chunk_offset, child_state, list_size,
                                                 child_type, -1);
    return;
}
```

`start_offset == 0` with `list_size == 0` only happens when no earlier row had elements, so it is reached only by an empty first chunk. A dictionary-encoded child reaches it despite the debug-only assert, and it is converted as a plain column. For a dictionary child, `child_type` is the index type, which [`arrow_duck_schema.cpp#L80-L81`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/v1.5.6/src/function/table/arrow/arrow_duck_schema.cpp#L80-L81) builds as `ArrowType(INTEGER)` with no `type_info`. The `VARCHAR` branch then calls `arrow_type.GetTypeInfo<ArrowStringInfo>()` ([`arrow_conversion.cpp#L846`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/v1.5.6/src/function/table/arrow_conversion.cpp#L846)) on that null `type_info`. The WASM build presumably doesn't trap the null read, which would explain its type-mismatch message instead of the null-dereference error.

### To Reproduce

```python
import duckdb
import pyarrow as pa

# 2049 rows: the first 2048 lists are empty, the last holds one value.
offsets = pa.array([0] * 2049 + [1], pa.int32())
child = pa.array(["a"]).dictionary_encode()  # dictionary<values=string, indices=int32>
tbl = pa.table({"l": pa.ListArray.from_arrays(offsets, child)})

print(duckdb.sql("SELECT * FROM tbl").fetchall()[-1])
```

Result: `_duckdb.InternalException: INTERNAL Error: Attempted to dereference unique_ptr that is NULL!`

Expected: `(['a'],)`, which is what you get after removing `.dictionary_encode()`.

### OS:

macOS 27.0, arm64

### DuckDB Version:

1.5.6 (also 1.4.0, and the same code is on `main` at 8681dc52)

### DuckDB Client:

Python (pyarrow 25.0.1); also DuckDB-WASM 1.31.0

### Hardware:

Apple Silicon

### Full Name:

Oliver Kaisti

### Affiliation:

Sitedrive

### Did you include all relevant configuration (e.g., CPU architecture, Linux distribution) to reproduce the issue?

- [x] Yes, I have

### Did you include all code required to reproduce the issue?

- [x] Yes, I have

### Did you include all relevant data sets for reproducing the issue?

Yes (the script generates its own data)

issue.title: Fix Arrow scan of list<dictionary> when the first chunk has no list elements

repository.name: duckdb
repository.description: DuckDB is a high-performance analytical database system

issue.body:
Fixes #26272.

The empty-list shortcut in `ArrowToDuckDBList` converted the child as a plain column, which breaks when the child is dictionary-encoded: it's read with its index type, which has no type info. I removed the shortcut, since the switch below already handles empty lists for every physical type (that's the path taken when the empty chunk isn't the first one).

Added a test with the reporter's case (2048 empty lists followed by one with a value), plus a control where the empty chunk comes second.

CI on my fork is green except `Deploy extensions`, where `check-extension-entries` wants a new httpfs setting (`s3_list_concurrency`) in `extension_entries.hpp`, unrelated to this change.

issue.title: Scan an Arrow list with an encoded child when its first chunk holds no elements

repository.name: duckdb
repository.description: DuckDB is a high-performance analytical database system

issue.body:
Scanning an Arrow `list<dictionary<int32, string>>` column failed with `INTERNAL Error: Attempted to dereference unique_ptr that is NULL!` when the first 2048 rows had no list elements and later rows did, for example 2048 empty lists followed by `['a']`. This was reported from Python (pyarrow) in duckdb/duckdb#26272, including on v1.5.6. In DuckDB-WASM, it invalidated the database.

`ArrowToDuckDBList` had a shortcut for chunks containing only empty lists starting at child offset 0. It converted the child as a plain column, guarded by `D_ASSERT(!child_array.dictionary)` only in debug builds. A dictionary child’s Arrow type describes its indices and carries no string type information, so VARCHAR conversion dereferenced a null `ArrowStringInfo`. The shortcut also skipped the run-end encoded path.

This removes the shortcut; the general path already handles empty slices of plain, dictionary and run-end encoded children. New tests scan lists with an all-empty first chunk: string dictionary values in `test/arrow/arrow_dict_nested_offset.cpp` and a run-end encoded child in `test/arrow/arrow_run_end_encoded.cpp`. The dictionary test fails on `main`; both pass with the change. Arrow tests pass on reldebug and relassert with sanitizers. All reldebug unit tests pass except failures also seen on `main`. Another contributor’s open duckdb/duckdb#26394 removes the same shortcut; this PR adds tests for the reported string dictionary case and run-end encoding.

Fixes duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#76
Fixes #26272

issue.title: Fix Arrow scans of run-end encoded list children and empty list dictionaries

repository.name: duckdb
repository.description: DuckDB is a high-performance analytical database system

issue.body:
Fixes Arrow scans of lists whose first chunk holds no elements and of fixed-size lists with a run-end encoded child, and adds tests for run-end encoded filters and NULL indices in dictionaries of unions.

Combines the PRs labeled `Ready To Merge` in https://github.com/duckdb-bot/duckdb/pulls below, on top of the current head of `main`. The changes of each PR are applied as one squashed commit.

duckdb-bot/duckdb#36 removes the early return for lists without elements in `ArrowToDuckDBList`, which duckdb-bot/duckdb#144 changed to skip run-end encoded children. Removing it covers both, and the tests of both PRs are kept.

## Changes applied (4 PRs)

- duckdb-bot/duckdb#36: Scan an Arrow list with an encoded child when its first chunk holds no elements
- duckdb-bot/duckdb#144: Decode a run-end encoded child of a fixed-size list in an Arrow scan
- duckdb-bot/duckdb#133: Test Arrow scan filters on tables with run-end encoded strings and integers
- duckdb-bot/duckdb#103: Test VARCHAR casts, union_tag and union_extract with NULL indices in Arrow dictionaries of unions

## Original descriptions

<details><summary>duckdb-bot/duckdb#36: Scan an Arrow list with an encoded child when its first chunk holds no elements</summary>

Moved from duckdb/duckdb#27356.

Scanning an Arrow `list<dictionary<int32, string>>` column failed with `INTERNAL Error: Attempted to dereference unique_ptr that is NULL!` when the first 2048 rows had no list elements and later rows did, for example 2048 empty lists followed by `['a']`. This was reported from Python (pyarrow) in duckdb/duckdb#26272, including on v1.5.6. In DuckDB-WASM, it invalidated the database.

`ArrowToDuckDBList` had a shortcut for chunks containing only empty lists starting at child offset 0. It converted the child as a plain column, guarded by `D_ASSERT(!child_array.dictionary)` only in debug builds. A dictionary child’s Arrow type describes its indices and carries no string type information, so VARCHAR conversion dereferenced a null `ArrowStringInfo`. The shortcut also skipped the run-end encoded path.

This removes the shortcut; the general path already handles empty slices of plain, dictionary and run-end encoded children. New tests scan lists with an all-empty first chunk: string dictionary values in `test/arrow/arrow_dict_nested_offset.cpp` and a run-end encoded child in `test/arrow/arrow_run_end_encoded.cpp`. The dictionary test fails on `main`; both pass with the change. Arrow tests pass on reldebug and relassert with sanitizers. All reldebug unit tests pass except failures also seen on `main`. Another contributor’s open duckdb/duckdb#26394 removes the same shortcut; this PR adds tests for the reported string dictionary case and run-end encoding.

Fixes duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#76
Related: duckdb/duckdb#26272

</details>

<details><summary>duckdb-bot/duckdb#144: Decode a run-end encoded child of a fixed-size list in an Arrow scan</summary>

We found that scanning Arrow data with a fixed-size list column (`+w:N`) whose child is run-end encoded (`+r`), for example through `duckdb_arrow_scan`, returned wrong values or crashed with a segmentation fault. The column binds as the values' type, such as `INTEGER[2]`, so nothing fails before the scan.

In `src/function/table/arrow_conversion.cpp`, `ArrowToDuckDBArray` only checked `child_array.dictionary` and otherwise called `ColumnArrowToDuckDB`. This read the run-end encoded child, a struct of run ends and values with a single buffer, as a plain array. `ArrowToDuckDBList` already dispatches on the child's physical type and decodes this child with `ColumnArrowToDuckDBRunEndEncoded`.

`ArrowToDuckDBArray` now uses `ColumnArrowToDuckDBRunEndEncoded` and reapplies parent-row NULLs to the child afterward, because decoding sets every child row's validity. Empty-child shortcuts in `ArrowToDuckDBArray` and `ArrowToDuckDBList` also send run-end encoded children to the decoder with zero rows, avoiding plain conversion's read of a values buffer those arrays do not have. Tests in `test/arrow/arrow_run_end_encoded.cpp` cover a small `FIXED_SIZE_LIST` with a run-end encoded child (wrong values on `main`), one crossing vector chunks with an array offset and a NULL run (crashes on `main`), and NULL rows over values outside the `TINYINT` range cast in a query over the scan (fails on `main`). Tests also cover `LIST` and `LIST(FIXED_SIZE_LIST)` columns containing only empty lists; these pass on `main` too because the extra read happens to stay inside the test's arrays. The `[arrow]` tests pass on reldebug and on relassert with sanitizers. All unit tests pass on reldebug except failures also present on `main` on this machine. No benchmark was run: the change adds one branch per vector of a fixed-size list. A run-end encoded values child of a run-end encoded array, and ancestor offsets lost through nested structs, remain unaddressed because they use separate paths. We found no earlier pull requests in duckdb/duckdb.

Fixes duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#580

</details>

<details><summary>duckdb-bot/duckdb#133: Test Arrow scan filters on tables with run-end encoded strings and integers</summary>

Filtering an Arrow table with run-end encoded strings failed during planning with `INTERNAL Error: Failed to cast ArrowTypeInfo, type mismatch (expected: STRING, got: STRUCT)`, even on a plain column: `SELECT i FROM t WHERE i > 1`. Unfiltered selects worked. duckdb/duckdb#27319 fixed this on main, so this pull request now only adds tests. duckdb/duckdb-python#666 reports the same bug.

A run-end encoded column uses its values' DuckDB type, but its type info holds both run ends and values. The pushdown check in `src/function/table/arrow.cpp` switched on that type and tried to cast this info to string info, which threw. Main now checks the encoding before reading type info and keeps every filter above scans containing run-end encoded columns, as for string and binary views, because PyArrow cannot filter these arrays. Main's tests in `test/arrow/arrow_filter_pushdown.cpp` verify that producers receive no filter. They filter encoded int32 directly and plain columns alongside encoded int32, encoded utf8, or lists of encoded utf8, returning only plain columns. They leave direct string filters, combined plain and encoded filters, and decoded values after filtering unchecked.

This pull request adds “Arrow scan of a table with a run-end encoded column and a filter” to `test/arrow/arrow_run_end_encoded.cpp`. It tests filters on plain int32, encoded utf8 strings (`r = 'a'`), and both combined, returning only the plain column. Two further queries filter plain columns alongside encoded int32 or lists of encoded int32, also returning the encoded column and checking its decoded values. Every query checks rows and row count. The new `RunEndStringColumn` helper builds the encoded parent with no buffers (`n_buffers` 0), as the Arrow C data interface requires; PyArrow 26 rejects one buffer. The test passes on main and in reldebug and relassert (sanitizer) builds. All reldebug unit tests pass except `test/sql/settings/reset/reset_threads.test`, which also fails on main under our runner's thread limit.

Related: duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#222

</details>

<details><summary>duckdb-bot/duckdb#103: Test VARCHAR casts, union_tag and union_extract with NULL indices in Arrow dictionaries of unions</summary>

An Arrow dictionary column with sparse union values gave inconsistent results for a NULL index: `x IS NULL` was true, but `x::VARCHAR` and `union_extract(x, 'd')` returned `0`, and `union_tag(x)` returned the first member. All three should return NULL. They now do on main, following duckdb/duckdb@61e8a48a0f5, merged with duckdb/duckdb#27575.

`ArrowToDuckDBConversion::ColumnArrowToDuckDBDictionary` converts dictionary values into a vector with an extra NULL sentinel slot for NULL indices. Previously, it marked only the slot's top-level validity NULL, leaving the union tag and members unchanged. Union functions read the tag, so the row appeared as the first member with value `0`. Main now flattens the values with `FlattenForSetNull` and calls `FlatVector::SetNull` on the sentinel for every value type. A union is internally a struct, so its tag and members are now NULL too.

After merging main, this PR only adds a C++ regression test in `test/arrow/arrow_union_offset.cpp`. Its original union-only `FlatVector::SetNull` call duplicated main's and was dropped during the merge, leaving no changes to `src/function/table/arrow_conversion.cpp`. The test builds a dictionary of sparse unions through the Arrow C data interface, including a dictionary-encoded member and a NULL index. A new optional projection in `ScanMatches` checks the cast, tag and extraction of both members. Main's tests in `test/arrow/arrow_dictionary_sentinel.cpp` cover struct, list, array and null type values, but no union. The new test passes on main and fails with the old behavior of marking only the sentinel's top-level validity NULL. The `[arrow]` tests, including the C API Arrow tests, pass in reldebug and relassert. The full reldebug unit suite fails only in `test/sql/settings/reset/reset_threads.test`, which also fails on main.

Related: duckdblabs/bot-issue-tracker#544

</details>
